problem.title1: What you write leaves your machine.
problem.title2: And the price, you find out later.
problem.body: That is what happens when the tool owns the infrastructure: your code goes to the servers of whoever sold you the editor, and the cost comes wrapped in a subscription that never tells you which run spent what.
problem.lead: In Axyoma, both are your call.
problem.ondeBody: With your own key, the turn goes straight from your machine to the provider. With a local model, it never leaves your machine — and that is in the free plan. In both cases, what you write does not pass through our servers.
problem.quantoTitle: What it costs, before it runs
problem.quantoBody: You see which model will run and how much that run consumes before you confirm. The charge shows up immediately, tied to the model that ran — and purchased credits never expire.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.oqueA: Axyoma is an open platform for working with AI agents across hundreds of models in a single application. It runs as a desktop app, next to your editor and your terminal.
faq.apiQ: Do I need to set up an API key?
faq.apiA: No. You can start right away with the credits included. If you prefer, you can also connect your own OpenRouter or OpenAI key.
faq.byokQ: Can I use my own API key?
faq.byokA: Yes, from OpenRouter or OpenAI. Under Settings → Models you paste the key and pick which models to use with it. Anything running through that key is billed by the provider, directly to you, and consumes no Axyoma credits. Anthropic with your own key is on the way.
faq.ondeChaveQ: Where is my API key stored?
faq.ondeChaveA: On your machine, encrypted, alongside the app's other credentials. It is never written to our servers: it travels encrypted on each request, is used in memory to talk to the provider and is discarded right after — it never lands in a log, a database or a backup. To remove it, clear the field under Settings → Models; it disappears from your computer and no copy exists anywhere else.
faq.localQ: Can I run models on my own machine?
faq.localA: Yes, at no cost. Axyoma talks to Ollama: install it from the app itself, download whichever model you want from the library and it shows up in the picker like any other. It runs offline, never touches our servers and spends no credits. The app warns you when a model does not fit in your machine's memory.
faq.escolherQ: Can I choose which model is used?
faq.escolherA: Yes. Pick the right model for each task by hand, or switch between providers based on cost, speed or quality — Gemini, Claude, GPT, Grok, Llama, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Mistral and more.
faq.autonomiaQ: Does the agent run actions automatically?
faq.autonomiaA: You set the level of autonomy. Whenever it matters, Axyoma asks for your approval before running an important action.
faq.cobrancaA: You can use Axyoma credits, buy extra credits or use your own API key. The cost of each run is shown transparently. One credit costs R$ 0.30 and you pay via Pix — by QR code, copy-and-paste or straight from your bank through Open Finance. Bonus and allowance credits are valid for Vertex AI models; purchased credits are valid for every model.
faq.sistemasA: Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel). Updates are automatic on Windows; on macOS the app tells you when a new version is out. The Linux build is coming back soon.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: A quick guide to installing, understanding and getting the most out of Axyoma AI. For a full tour of what it does, see the Features page.
docs.instalacaoBody: Download the app on the <download>download page</download> — the button detects your system. Once installed, sign in with your Axyoma account (the same one as the site).
docs.instalacaoMacos: Download the .dmg (Apple Silicon or Intel) from the download page, drag Axyoma into the Applications folder and open it. When an update is out, the app tells you to download the new version.
docs.instalacaoWindows: Download the .exe installer, run it and follow the wizard. The app updates itself in the background.
docs.instalacaoLinux: The Linux installer is temporarily unavailable and is coming back soon. In the meantime, Axyoma runs on macOS and Windows.
docs.loginBody: Sign in with email and password or with your Google account — the app login is the same as the site's. If you forget your password, use the recovery option on the sign-in screen. The account area shows your plan, credit balance and usage history.
docs.modeloBody: Under Settings → Models, add the models you want to see in the chat picker. While you work, switch models per task straight from the picker at the top — no reconfiguration and no API key. The catalog includes Gemini, Claude, GPT, Grok, Llama, DeepSeek, Kimi and more.
docs.modosDesign: Pick Design mode in the top selector, describe the artwork you want (post, carousel, motion or template), generate it, adjust the result and export. Available on paid plans.
docs.modosPlan: In Plan mode, describe the feature. Axyoma breaks it into tasks and puts together a plan. Review it, edit it if you want and approve — only then does execution start.
docs.modosCode: In Code mode, hand the task to the agent. It reads and edits files, runs commands, debugs and shows every action on the timeline. Use the built-in terminal and editor to follow along and step in whenever you want. At the end, it can open the PR on GitHub.
docs.creditosBody1: Usage is charged in credits (1 credit = R$ 0.30), calculated from the model's real cost. Every new account gets 100 bonus credits to try things out.
docs.creditosBody2: Bonus credits and the plans' allowance credits are valid for Vertex AI (Google Cloud) models. Purchased credits are valid for every model, including Vertex ones. To buy, use the Account tab (in the app or on the site) and pay via Pix. Track how much each turn consumed under Account → Recent usage.
docs.ajudaBody: Still have a question, or ran into a problem? Talk to us through the <contato>contact</contato> page. More documentation is on the way.

recursos.title: Features
recursos.intro: Axyoma AI is an AI engineering studio in a desktop app. In one place you design, plan and program — with the best models and credits you control. Here is everything it does, in detail.
recursos.modosBody: The product revolves around three modes, switched from a selector at the top of the app. Each one covers a different stage of your work.
recursos.modosDesign: Artwork for social media — posts, carousels, motion pieces and templates. You describe the idea, the AI designs it, you adjust the result and publish. It is the fastest way to go from brief to finished artwork without opening a separate editor. Design mode is exclusive to paid plans.
recursos.modosPlan: Planning before coding. Instead of turning loose an agent that does everything at once, Axyoma breaks the feature into tasks, builds a plan you read and review, and only executes after your approval. You keep control step by step and see exactly what will happen before it happens.
recursos.modosCode: A coding agent that executes end to end. It reads, writes and edits files in any language or framework, runs commands (tests, lint, build, migrations), debugs by reading its own logs and delivers the work — right up to opening the pull request on GitHub. It ships with a built-in terminal, the Monaco editor and a visual timeline of every action the agent takes, so you can follow everything in real time.
recursos.ferramentasBody: In Code mode, the agent does not just suggest — it acts. For that it has a set of tools that operate directly on your project:
recursos.ferramentaArquivos: Reads, writes and edits your project's files, in any language or framework.
recursos.ferramentaComandos: Runs tests, lint, build, migrations and any terminal command — and reads the output to correct itself.
recursos.ferramentaDepuracao: Investigates errors by reading the logs and adjusts the code until it works.
recursos.ferramentaBusca: Queries the web when it needs context, documentation or an up-to-date reference.
recursos.ferramentaScreenshot: Captures the screen to inspect interfaces and visual results.
recursos.ferramentaSubagentes: Delegates parts of the task to other models — or puts several of them in competition for the best solution.
recursos.ferramentaSkills: Runs reusable commands and instructions that you write yourself.
recursos.modelosBody: Axyoma brings the world's leading models together in a single picker — Gemini, Claude, GPT, Grok, Llama, DeepSeek, Kimi and more. You choose the best model for each task without leaving the app and without managing an API key per provider. Need heavy reasoning in one step and speed in another? Just switch the model in the picker.
recursos.creditosBody1: You do not need your own API key: you use Axyoma credits. Each credit is worth R$ 0.30 and the charge is calculated from the real cost (in US dollars) of the model you picked — you pay for what you consume, with no artificial ceiling and no surprises.
recursos.creditosBody2: Every new account gets 100 bonus credits at sign-up — in practice, a month of the Pro plan to try the platform freely. When the credits run out, you buy more or subscribe to a plan.
recursos.creditosBody3: One important rule: bonus credits and the plans' allowance credits (Pro and Teams) are valid for Vertex AI (Google Cloud) models. Purchased credits are valid for every model, Vertex included. So you test at no cost and unlock the whole catalog whenever you want.
recursos.skillsBody: Skills are reusable commands and instructions you write once and call whenever you need them. Standardise a review flow, a commit format, a response style — and let the agent repeat it your way, without you rewriting the instruction every time.
recursos.githubBody: Axyoma connects to GitHub to close the loop: the agent creates and updates pull requests and exports the project straight from the app. You go from planning to PR without switching tools.
recursos.plataformasTitle: Cross-platform and always up to date
recursos.plataformasBody: The app runs on macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows. On Windows it updates itself; on macOS it tells you when a new version is available to download. You always work on the latest version, effortlessly. The Linux build is coming back soon.
recursos.vantagemChaves: You create the account, get credits and use it. No configuring providers or pasting keys.
recursos.vantagemUsoNome: You only pay for what you use
recursos.vantagemUso: The charge follows the model's real consumption. No mandatory subscription to get started.
recursos.vantagemModelos: Switch models per task without switching apps.
recursos.vantagemAgente: From the plan to the PR, the work happens inside the app.
recursos.vantagemControle: Plan mode reviews before acting: nothing runs without your approval.
recursos.vantagemMulti: macOS and Windows, with automatic updates.

contato.title: About and Contact
contato.intro: What Axyoma is, how it works and how to reach us.
contato.sobreBody1: {produto} is an AI engineering studio for developers, makers, agencies and freelancers. Instead of only suggesting, the agent executes: it reads and writes files, runs tests, lint, build and migrations, debugs by reading logs and delivers the result — with a built-in terminal, a code editor and GitHub integration. All on a credit model you control, with no infrastructure to set up and no API keys to manage.
contato.sobreBody2: Want the detail of everything it does? See the <recursos>Features</recursos> page.
contato.faqOqueA: An AI engineering studio in a desktop app (macOS and Windows). In a single app you create social media artwork (Design mode), break features into reviewable tasks (Plan mode) and run an agent that reads, writes and edits code, runs commands and delivers all the way to the PR on GitHub (Code mode).
contato.faqCreditosA: You do not need your own API key. You use Axyoma credits, where 1 credit = R$ 0.30, and the charge is calculated from the real cost (in USD) of the model you picked. Every new account gets 100 bonus credits to try things out. Bonus credits and the plans' allowance credits (Pro and Teams) are valid for Vertex AI (Google Cloud) models; purchased credits are valid for every model, Vertex included.
contato.faqModelosQ: Which AI models can I use?
contato.faqModelosA: A catalog with the market's leading models in a single picker — Gemini, Claude, GPT, Grok, Llama, DeepSeek, Kimi and more. Google models (Vertex AI) are reached with bonus and allowance credits; for every other model, use purchased credits (which work everywhere).
contato.faqPlanosA: Free: 100 bonus credits at sign-up, to try things out. Free also includes your own key (OpenRouter and OpenAI) and local models through Ollama, which consume no credits. Pro and Teams (coming soon): paid plans with allowance credits and Design mode; prices will be announced at launch. Bonus and allowance credits are valid for Vertex AI models; purchased credits are valid for every model.
contato.faqSistemasQ: Which systems does it run on?
contato.faqSistemasA: macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows. The app keeps itself updated on Windows; on macOS it notifies you when a new version is out. The Linux build is coming back soon.
contato.faqPagamentoA: Via Pix — QR code, copy-and-paste or payment straight from your bank (Open Finance) — at checkout on the site or in the app.
